relationship: A rounded measurement represents an interval, and calculated bounds must use the extremal values that make the stated claim hardest to certify.

learnerLoop.action: Scrub true readings to discover rounding boundaries, drag distance and time to find speed extremes, prove the claim, then test finer measurements.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Rounded displays change as true values cross interval endpoints; dragging allowed distance and time updates the derived speed.
learnerLoop.evidence: The interval model, extremal case and certification check reveal whether the claim follows.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Choose the upper or lower bound that tests the claim conservatively.

invariants: A rounded value includes all values in its rounding interval.
A guarantee requires the extremal case that works against the claim.
safeAdaptations: Vary rounding units and positive measurement scenarios.
Adjust calculation support while retaining boundary discovery, direct speed exploration, the worst-case proof and the finer-precision comparison.
nonGoals: Certifying a claim from the rounded displayed values alone.

task.description: Current problem statement and supplied quantities.
task.visibility: Shown at the start of each problem or stage.

model.description: Operated construction and its live measurements; see quantities for what is given and revealed.
model.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

working.description: Ordered calculations, learner entries and consequential evidence for the current task.
working.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

completion.description: Achievement, next task or learning transition.
completion.visibility: Shown only when the local completion conditions below are satisfied; representation controls are separately identified.

stage-settings.description: Existing stage navigation, Working level and current-step reset.
stage-settings.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

rounding-readouts.description: Inline seven-segment rounded readings preserve trailing zeros for the current precision; adjacent true-value labels and interval markers show the hidden measurement range.
rounding-readouts.visibility: Present in every stage; stage 0 readings change at crossed boundaries; later stages retain the recorded readings.

proof-evidence.description: Distinct diamonds show the learner-entered coarse distance/time proof values against fixed half-open intervals.
proof-evidence.visibility: Stage 3, Working All, when each entered quantity is numeric and inside the ruler domain.

interval-check.description: Validate the four finer interval limits before the final speed proof.

distance-time.description: Two underlying measurements with four interval endpoints. Endpoints are bounds of these measurements, not four unrelated physical quantities.
distance-time.domain: Distance m; time s; intervals are lower-inclusive and upper-exclusive.
distance-time.source: Reported values and rounding units are given; stage 0 discovers both edges with rulers.
distance-time.output: Rounded readings change at crossed boundaries. Included/excluded endpoint markers show half-open intervals. Stage 3 entries add proof markers; stage 4 proposed limits appear before checking. Once finer intervals are accepted or supplied, the model uses the lower distance and a time just below the excluded upper limit.

worst-case-speed.description: Lower speed bound uses lower distance divided by upper time; upper speed uses the opposite endpoints.
worst-case-speed.domain: m/s; numerical proof uses endpoint limits while the draggable upper endpoint is approached from below.
worst-case-speed.source: Physical extremes are explored first, then working is supplied or entered by level.
worst-case-speed.output: The proof and speed-range display compare the lower bound with 8.05.

certificate.description: One yes/no assertion for each precision: whether every allowed run meets the threshold.
certificate.source: Learner chooses at every Working level.
certificate.output: Explicit Check prediction verifies arithmetic and verdict together.

modes.none: Discover interval boundaries and speed extremes physically; proof arithmetic is supplied, but the certificate verdict still requires a learner choice/check.
modes.some: Interval values are supplied; learner enters lower speed and verdict.
modes.all: Learner supplies coarse lower distance/upper time/speed and verdict; the finer stage first requires all four new interval limits.
modes.precision: Base readings are 100 m to 1 m and 12.4 s to 0.1 s; the final stage tightens to 0.1 m and 0.01 s. The speed threshold remains 8.05 m/s.

dependencies: Both distance and time boundaries must be crossed before interval discovery completes.
Both fastest and slowest endpoint combinations must be explored in stage 1.
Coarse proof precedes finer precision; All gates the final proof behind four correct finer interval limits.
implementation.completion: state.complete[0..3] records discovery, both extremes, successful coarse proof (no guarantee), and successful finer proof (guarantee). Completion is hidden during dragging.
limitations: The fixed task is a certificate counterexample/proof, not a generated set of independent measurement questions. Numeric parsing uses the existing parseFloat/tolerance checks.
